title: सरकारका पछिल्ला गतिविधिहरू सत्ताकब्जाको संकेतः रविन्द्र मिश्र
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौँ । राष्ट्रिय प्रजातन्त्र पार्टीका वरिष्ठ नेता रविन्द्र मिश्रले न्यायालय र बिचौलिया प्रकरणलाई लिएर गम्भीर प्रश्न उठाएका छन् । उनले समाचार कक्षबाट पत्रकार पक्राउ पर्ने, पूर्वप्रधानन्यायाधीश पक्राउ पर्ने र व्यापारीका घरमा खानतलासी हुने घटनालाई जोड्दै वर्तमान सत्ता संरचनाको प्रभाव र नियन्त्रणबारे प्रश्न गरेका हुन् । फेसबुकमा आफ्नो धारणा राख्दै मिश्रले पछिल्लो घटनाक्रमलाई सामान्य रूपमा लिन नहुने बताएका छन् । ‘पत्रकार छुट्नै पर्थ्यो, छुटे । तर गम्भीर चिन्ताको विषय अरू छन्,’ भन्दै उनले विभिन्न घटनाको सूची प्रस्तुत गरेका छन् । मिश्रले समाचार कक्षबाट बिनापुर्जी पत्रकार पक्राउ परेको, मध्यरातमा बिना पुर्जी पूर्वप्रधानन्यायाधीश पक्राउ परेको, व्यापारीको घरमा खानतलासी गरिएको तथा दिनदहाडै व्यापारीहरू पक्राउ परेको उल्लेख गरेका छन् । त्यस्तै, विभिन्न मिडिया हाउस र राजनीतिक नेताहरूको घरअगाडि शङ्कास्पद रूपमा गाडी पार्क गरिएको विषय पनि उनले उठाएका छन् । उनले अख्तियार प्रमुखलाई प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयमै तर्साइएको उल्लेख गर्दै ‘आफ्नाको बचाउ गर, अरूलाई थर्काऊ’ भन्ने प्रवृत्तिमाथि पनि प्रश्न गरेका छन् । मिश्रले केही सत्ताधारीले सरकारको नियन्त्रणबारे सार्वजनिक रूपमा गर्ने दाबी र वास्तविक अवस्थाबीच अन्तर रहेको टिप्पणी गरेका छन् । ‘कतिपय सत्ताधारीहरू मिडियामा भन्छन्, हाम्रो नियन्त्रणमा अहिले संसद्को तल्लो सदनमात्र छ । राष्ट्रिय सभा, स्थानीय तह, कर्मचारीतन्त्र, न्यायालय, प्रहरी त पुरानै हुन्,’ उनले लेखेका छन् । यसको अप्रत्यक्ष अर्थ सत्ता अहिले पनि पूर्ण रूपमा आफ्नो नियन्त्रणमा नरहेको भन्ने रहेको मिश्रको टिप्पणी छ । उनले पछिल्लो समय भइरहेका घटनालाई सत्ता कब्जाका सङ्केतका रूपमा व्याख्या गरेका छन् । ‘पछिल्ला समयमा जे भइरहेका छन्, ती सत्ताकब्जाका सङ्केत हुन्,’ उनले लेखेका छन् । मिश्रले सत्ता कब्जा हुनु भनेको अहिले आलोचना वा विरोध गर्नेहरूले समेत भविष्यमा आफ्नो अवस्था बुझ्नुपर्ने दिन आउन सक्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन् । ‘सत्ताकब्जा हुनु भनेको आज ताली पिट्नेहरू पनि रुने दिन आउनु हो,’ उनको टिप्पणी छ । Kathmandu. Senior leader of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party, Rabindra Mishra, has raised serious questions regarding the judiciary and the middlemen issue. He has questioned the influence and control of the current power structure, linking the incidents of journalists being arrested from newsrooms, the arrest of former Chief Justices and searches at the homes of businessmen. Expressing his views on Facebook, Mishra said that the latest developments should not be taken lightly. "The journalist had to be released, and he was released. But there are other issues of serious concern," he said, presenting a list of various incidents. Mishra mentioned that journalists were arrested without a warrant from the newsroom, a former Chief Justice was arrested without a warrant in the middle of the night, a businessman's house was searched, and businessmen were arrested in broad daylight. He also raised the issue of suspiciously parked vehicles in front of the houses of various media houses and political leaders. He also questioned the trend of 'protect yourself, intimidate others', mentioning that the head of the CIAA was intimidated in the Prime Minister's Office. Mishra has commented that there is a gap between the public claims made by some in power about government control and the actual situation. "Some in power say in the media that we now only have the lower house of parliament under our control. The National Assembly, local levels, bureaucracy, judiciary, and police are the same," he wrote. Mishra comments that this indirectly means that the government is still not fully under its control. He has interpreted recent events as signs of a power grab. "What has been happening recently is a sign of a power grab," he wrote. Mishra has warned that even those who criticize or oppose the seizure of power now may have to understand their situation in the future. "Seizing power means that even those who applaud today will cry," he comments.

उनले पछिल्लो समय भइरहेका घटनालाई सत्ता कब्जाका सङ्केतका रूपमा व्याख्या गरेका छन् ।

‘पछिल्ला समयमा जे भइरहेका छन्, ती सत्ताकब्जाका सङ्केत हुन्,’ उनले लेखेका छन् ।

मिश्रले सत्ता कब्जा हुनु भनेको अहिले आलोचना वा विरोध गर्नेहरूले समेत भविष्यमा आफ्नो अवस्था बुझ्नुपर्ने दिन आउन सक्ने चेतावनी दिएका छन् ।

‘सत्ताकब्जा हुनु भनेको आज ताली पिट्नेहरू पनि रुने दिन आउनु हो,’ उनको टिप्पणी छ ।

Kathmandu. Senior leader of the Rastriya Prajatantra Party, Rabindra Mishra, has raised serious questions regarding the judiciary and the middlemen issue. He has questioned the influence and control of the current power structure, linking the incidents of journalists being arrested from newsrooms, the arrest of former Chief Justices and searches at the homes of businessmen. Expressing his views on Facebook, Mishra said that the latest developments should not be taken lightly. "The journalist had to be released, and he was released. But there are other issues of serious concern," he said, presenting a list of various incidents. Mishra mentioned that journalists were arrested without a warrant from the newsroom, a former Chief Justice was arrested without a warrant in the middle of the night, a businessman's house was searched, and businessmen were arrested in broad daylight. He also raised the issue of suspiciously parked vehicles in front of the houses of various media houses and political leaders. He also questioned the trend of 'protect yourself, intimidate others', mentioning that the head of the CIAA was intimidated in the Prime Minister's Office. Mishra has commented that there is a gap between the public claims made by some in power about government control and the actual situation. "Some in power say in the media that we now only have the lower house of parliament under our control. The National Assembly, local levels, bureaucracy, judiciary, and police are the same," he wrote. Mishra comments that this indirectly means that the government is still not fully under its control. He has interpreted recent events as signs of a power grab. "What has been happening recently is a sign of a power grab," he wrote. Mishra has warned that even those who criticize or oppose the seizure of power now may have to understand their situation in the future. "Seizing power means that even those who applaud today will cry," he comments.
